summary.name: Engineering Reliable Mobile Applications
summary.one_liner: A Google SRE report on applying site reliability engineering concepts and tools to client-side code, especially native mobile apps.
keywords: how to make mobile app reliable
use_cases: making a mobile app more reliable
investigating user reports of poor availability
applying SRE practices to client applications
summary.what_it_does: The page is the introduction to a Google SRE report on engineering reliable mobile applications, written by Kristine Chen, Venkat Patnala, Devin Carraway and Pranjal Deo with Jessie Yang. It argues that services can report healthy while users still experience poor availability through client apps on their phones. It notes that SRE has traditionally focused on systems run in datacenters rather than code running on the client. The report explains why client-side reliability matters, describes the challenges of that environment, and offers SRE concepts and potential tools for client applications. The visible excerpt does not list specific techniques beyond this overview.
notable: Covers client-side reliability, which traditional datacenter-focused SRE often misses
Written by Google SRE authors (Chen, Patnala, Carraway, Deo, with Yang)
Listed in the awesome-sre resource collection under Books
caveats: Only the introduction is shown; specific methods and tools are not visible in the page text
Platform coverage is implied by the mobile focus rather than explicitly listed
